title: Decode RFC 2047 encoded-words in extract_headers
description:
extract_headers() in parse.rs slices raw bytes via h.offset_start/h.offset_end and applies from_utf8_lossy, leaving encoded-words like =?utf-8?b?SGVsbG8=?= undecoded in ParsedMessage.headers.

mail-parser has an internal RFC 2047 decoder (decoders/encoded_word.rs, decode_rfc2047) but mime-tree bypasses it by reading raw offsets. Fix: use mail-parser's decoded header value instead of the raw byte slice, so callers see decoded Unicode strings in ParsedMessage.headers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Subject: =?utf-8?b?SGVsbG8=?= appears as 'Hello' in ParsedMessage.headers
- Subject: =?iso-8859-1?q?caf=E9?= appears as 'café'
- Headers with no encoded-words are unchanged
- Add tests for both cases with known decoded values as oracle (NOT derived from this crate — use https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2047 examples or manual decode)
